findings.reason: the referent is the refusal, not `pull`, so the misreading is resolved by the adjacent signature and only a wording clause would change.
findings.text: the accounting sentence "Its one option, `--force`, is the escape that refusal needs" reads as if `pull` has one option, while the signature three lines above declares `[--version] [--dest DIR] [--force]`

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `imas_ambix/maps_cli.py` hides the semver state machine, the registry client, the tree digest and the push/pull/status commands behind one `imas-ambix maps` group, and the four copied ghcr.py functions are justified by the graph-stack import they avoid.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the machine-to-package table is placed in `imas_ambix/data/paths.py` beside the `MAPS_DIR` that already owns the map path (:35); the census shows the package name and legacy tag written only at `imasdb.sh:44`, so no second owner is forked.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §18's accounting paragraph names the installer's private pull it merges into `maps pull`, states why `release` and `status` are capabilities with nothing to retire, and the newly declared `--force` is named as the escape the `pull` refusal needs.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §18's registry calls are cited to `imas_codex/graph/ghcr.py` (`list_registry_tags`:335, `fetch_tag_messages`:355, `login_to_ghcr`:230, `require_oras`:205) and its push convention to `imas_codex/graph/remote.py:1084-1089`, and both match the code opened; ambix has no registry or version-tag machinery to reuse (`grep` for `oras`/`ghcr`/tag queries returns only the installer).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one wrapper §18 adds is the installer's `oras pull`, and §18 states why it is merged rather than extended: `install/imasdb.sh:44,70` is the only site, and `maps pull` gives the registry, auth form and artifact type one owner.
